title: Upstream state (agent to router, binary frame OLLAMA, stream 0)
description: The agent's own observation of its upstream: installed models, loaded models, reachable or not. Sent at the start of each session, on every change, after approval and at least every 30 s. While a report is fresh (45 s) the router does not poll the node. A report without a boolean up, or with up true and tags or ps that are not lists, is dropped and the router polls again. Dropped before approval.

up.description: false: the upstream does not answer; the router takes the node offline at once.

error.description: Why the upstream counts as down (with up false), for display only.

rev.description: Revision counter, increases with every change; the router logs it.

ts.description: Unix seconds when the frame was sent. Informational; the router uses its receive time.

tags.description: Installed models: the entries of Ollama's /api/tags, unchanged. null counts as an empty list (agent 0.14.0 sent null).

ps.description: Loaded models: the entries of Ollama's /api/ps, unchanged. null counts as an empty list.

upstream_state.description: OpenAI-compatible upstream only: held (stopped on upstream-hold) or starting (not answering yet). Absent when it answers normally.

serving.description: ollama while the upstream is held and the standby Ollama answers in its place. Absent otherwise.

model.description: An entry as the upstream reports it. The router uses entries with a string name and ignores the rest. An OpenAI-compatible upstream's models are reported in this shape (name, size 0).

upstream_blocked.description: The agent did not start the held upstream on a release order and keeps it held. Cleared (absent) once the reason is gone.

reason.description: Fixed reason code; memory: RAM in use plus the upstream's need would exceed limit_percent.

need_gib.description: Remembered RAM need of the upstream in GiB.

limit_percent.description: Configured limit in percent of the RAM.
